skill.name: investigate-first
skill.description: Diagnose ambiguous failures before editing. Use for unknown causes, intermittent behavior, performance regressions, or investigations needing evidence-ranked hypotheses.
skill.summary: Investigate failures with evidence-ranked hypotheses before changing code.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The two prompt-only files contain no executable code, external access, credential handling, or suspicious instructions. No static or semantic security findings were identified.

content.value_statement: Premature edits can hide causes and introduce new failures. This skill organizes evidence, ranks hypotheses, and identifies a credible mechanism before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Separates observed symptoms from inferred causes.
Traces inputs, state transitions, ownership boundaries, and failure output.
Ranks hypotheses using available evidence and inexpensive falsification tests.
Delays product code edits until evidence supports a credible failure mechanism.
Reports the likely cause, supporting proof, or an exact investigation blocker.
limitations: Does not guarantee a root cause when evidence is incomplete.
Does not implement a fix unless the task explicitly authorizes changes.
Does not provide domain-specific debugging tools or executable diagnostics.
Depends on access to relevant logs, code, reproduction steps, and system context.

use_cases.title: Diagnose an Intermittent Test Failure
use_cases.description: Organize observations and rank likely mechanisms before modifying test or product code.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Performance Regression
use_cases.description: Trace changed inputs and state transitions to identify evidence supporting the slowdown.

use_cases.title: Clarify an Ambiguous Defect Report
use_cases.description: Separate reported symptoms from assumptions and define the next useful evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this failure before proposing edits: [symptom]. Separate observations from assumptions and list the evidence needed next.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the cause is unknown and available context is limited.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Root Cause Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [failure details]. Rank plausible causes by supporting evidence, conflicting evidence, and the cheapest test that could disprove each cause.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after collecting logs, error messages, or reproduction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the regression from [baseline] to [current behavior]. Trace inputs, state transitions, ownership boundaries, and outputs without changing code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when behavior changed after a release, configuration update, or dependency change.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence-Backed Diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [system context and evidence]. Identify the most credible mechanism, prove each causal step, and name the exact blocker if evidence remains insufficient.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex failures spanning multiple components or teams.

output_examples.input: The checkout test fails twice weekly, but reruns pass. Recent edits changed retry timing.
output: Observed: the first run sometimes times out, while immediate reruns pass.
Leading hypothesis: shared setup becomes ready after the first attempt.
Next test: record setup readiness and request timestamps on the first run.

output_examples.input: API latency increased after deployment, with no increase in request volume.
output_examples.output: The strongest evidence points to a new downstream wait. Compare dependency timing before and after deployment to confirm the responsible transition.

output_examples.input: A report is empty for one customer, but logs and sample data are unavailable.
output_examples.output: No cause can be supported yet. The exact blocker is missing customer-specific input, filtering decisions, and report generation output.

best_practices: Provide exact symptoms, timestamps, reproduction steps, and relevant recent changes.
Label observations, assumptions, and hypotheses separately.
Prefer inexpensive tests that can quickly disprove the leading explanation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat temporal correlation as proof of causation.
Do not edit multiple components before identifying a supported mechanism.
Do not continue exploring after evidence proves the cause or identifies the exact blocker.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for unknown causes, intermittent failures, performance regressions, or investigations with competing explanations.

faq.question: Will this skill edit my code?
faq.answer: It will not edit code unless your task explicitly authorizes implementation after diagnosis.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide symptoms, expected behavior, reproduction steps, logs, timestamps, recent changes, and relevant system boundaries.

faq.question: How does it rank hypotheses?
faq.answer: It compares each hypothesis with supporting evidence and prioritizes inexpensive tests that could disprove it.

faq.question: What happens when evidence is insufficient?
faq.answer: The skill identifies the exact missing evidence or access that blocks a credible diagnosis.

faq.question: Can it investigate performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It can trace inputs, state transitions, boundaries, and output timing to identify a supported regression mechanism.
